title: Tree From Traversals
statement:
Rebuild a binary tree from its preorder and inorder traversals.

Contract
- `preorder` and `inorder` are non-null arrays of the same length and describe the same binary tree.
- All values in the tree are distinct, so the two traversals identify exactly one tree.
- Return the root of the rebuilt tree using `Solution.TreeNode` (fields `value`, `left`, `right`), or `null` when both arrays are empty.
- Do not mutate the input arrays.

Examples
- `buildTree(new int[]{4, 2, 1, 3, 6, 5}, new int[]{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6})` returns the tree `[4, 2, 6, 1, 3, 5]` (level order).
- `buildTree(new int[]{7}, new int[]{7})` returns the single-node tree `[7]`.
- `buildTree(new int[]{1, 2, 3}, new int[]{3, 2, 1})` returns `[1, 2, null, 3]`, a chain leaning left.
hints: The first preorder value is always the root. Finding that value in the inorder array splits it into the left and right subtrees.
The number of values left of the root in inorder tells you how many preorder values belong to the left subtree; the rest belong to the right subtree.
Searching the inorder array for every root is slow; precompute a value-to-index map once. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space, where n is the number of nodes.
inputSyntax: Input: the preorder list followed by the inorder list, for example: [4, 2, 1, 3, 6, 5] [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
